{

  "outcome": "abstained",
  "answer": null,

    "query": "can two pytest sessions run at the same time here",
    "decision": "answer",

    "items": [
      {
        "chunk_id": "90b26b8b49c514cb4453caba1d16026b4699144a0810c1a2ff04532c66dfd20a",
        "text": "Two pytest sessions running at the same time against the same test database collide. `tests/conftest.py`\ncalls `apply_migrations` from a session fixture, and `recall.schema`'s guard refuses the second one:\n\nrecall.schema.ConcurrentMigrator: another RE-call schema migrator is already running\n\nThe loser does not fail one test. **Every** test errors at setup, so the run reports e.g.\n`3 skipped, 62 errors` with no failures at all. Reproduced deliberately on 2026-08-05 with three\nconcurrent runs of `tests/test_bench_systems.py`: one passed, two errored wholesale.",
        "source": "pytest-sessions-cannot-run-in-parallel.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-08-24T21:03:05.654848+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5924287085277622,
        "confidence": 0.96872858903498,
        "verdict": "ok"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "79d4f7138bbe3afa638457040d1c2af6de0e6b20e47ef71e17f705cbe448acf0",
        "text": "**How to apply:**\n1. A suite verdict is the SUMMARY LINE, never an exit code. An output file with no pytest output\n   means \"did not run or was lost\", whatever the code says.\n2. Launch long suites detached with their own log (`nohup python -u -m pytest tests/ -q > log\n   2>&1 &`, the `-u` matters or the log stays empty for minutes) and watch the log with a\n   Monitor until-loop for the summary line.\n3. Before relaunching anything DB-backed, list live python processes and match COMMAND LINES:\n   two suites on one session database invalidate each other silently.\n4. Distinguish your processes from other sessions' by command line before killing: this machine\n   routinely runs parallel sessions with their own suites.",
        "source": "background-suite-exit-0-with-empty-output-is-not-green.md",
        "ordinal": 2,
        "indexed_at": "2026-08-24T21:02:36.603638+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5683058839026711,
        "confidence": 0.9198692123473964,
        "verdict": "ok"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "aefa693b11a3901015aa3bd3ffff724f6f3170bb54c08ccb75418c9ad377506f",
        "text": "| Symptom | Cause |\n| --- | --- |\n| `ConcurrentMigrator` in fixture setup | two pytest processes contend for the schema-migration advisory lock; `scripts/ablate_store_latency_guards.py` documents it |\n| `LockNotAvailable: canceling statement due to lock timeout` | another session on the SAME container, still running |\n| `test_rate_limit_http.py`, `test_mcp_auth_http.py` | these stand up real HTTP servers and contend on PORTS; a private container does not protect them |\n| `FileNotFoundError` inside `tmp_path` | pytest keeps only the 3 most recent `pytest-of-<user>/pytest-<n>` roots and prunes older ones AT STARTUP, so a new run deletes the dirs of runs in flight |\n| pool / latency / backend-count assertions (\"pool churned: 3 distinct backends\u2026\") | CPU contention, not DB contention |\n|",
        "source": "concurrent-pytest-false-reds.md",
        "ordinal": 14,
        "indexed_at": "2026-08-24T21:02:41.179465+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.537134674958309,
        "confidence": 0.760933743895847,
        "verdict": "ok"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "639814e935a0470b83ab54288e94db52693a71cf4f61d955bfb2cfd87701cf45",
        "text": "**Why it matters:** the guard is working as designed, but its failure signature looks exactly like a\ncatastrophic breakage of the code under test. It cost me a wrong conclusion once: in a mutation-testing\nharness I counted two mutants as \"caught\" because the suite went red, when the redness was this\ncollision and not the mutant.\n\n**How to apply:** run pytest sessions in this repo **sequentially**, never overlapping. In any harness\nthat shells out to pytest in a loop, treat `errors` and `failed` as different evidence: only `failed`\nmeans a test caught something. Retry (or abort) on seeing `ConcurrentMigrator` in the output rather\nthan scoring that run. See also [[bench-systems-suite-spends-openrouter-credits]] for the other trap in\nthis same file.\n\n---",
        "source": "pytest-sessions-cannot-run-in-parallel.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-08-24T21:03:05.661840+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5553669929504434,
        "confidence": 0.8708062966551109,
        "verdict": "ok"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "53392d23c357668ee3c34aafccfe0892993aae957842fecdf0897bd48c5885ac",
        "text": "\u26a0\ufe0f **Extended 2026-08-18: the collision is not only the database, and the second one HANGS rather\nthan fails.** With three sessions on this machine running suites at once,\n`test_libreoffice_converts_legacy_office_sources` blocked inside `subprocess.run` until pytest's\nglobal timeout fired, and the run produced **no summary line at all**, so there was no verdict to\nread: not a pass, not a failure. LibreOffice refuses two instances against one user profile, so the\nsecond waits on a lock it can never get.",
        "source": "pytest-sessions-cannot-run-in-parallel.md",
        "ordinal": 3,

        "valid_from": null,

        "cosine": 0.5209720395257411,

        "verdict": "ok"
      }

payload:
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "outcome": "abstained",
  "answer": null,
  "clarification_request": null,
  "trusted_evidence": {
    "query": "what happens if I mix two embedding models in one tenant",
    "decision": "answer",
    "reason_code": null,
    "calibrated": true,
    "stale": false,
    "embedding_profile": "voyage:voyage-4",
    "retrieval_profile": "fast",
    "index_generation": "legacy",
    "items": [
      {
        "chunk_id": "f2440fbf349851c02d440bcfe19c1379d678a2bd43d2fe118b0a28ef7c847afc",
        "text": "\ud83d\udd11 **One embedding model per tenant.** Not a convention: it is the only thing standing between a\nmixed corpus and silently wrong retrieval. When a corpus wants a code model and a prose model,\nthat is two tenants, not one with two writers.\n\nFound on 2026-08-15 designing the `recall_repos` corpus on VPS2 (five repositories, code via\n`voyage-code-3`, docs via `voyage-4`). Ten tenants, `<repo>-code` and `<repo>-docs`, for exactly\nthis reason. The index driver asserts `code_embedder.dim == docs_embedder.dim` before writing,\nbecause both tenants share one table and one fixed vector width.\n\n\u26a0\ufe0f The same reasoning applies to the CHUNKER, but the failure is different and worse: see\n[[chunker-is-not-in-the-index-fingerprint]]. Related: [[guards-that-cannot-fail]],\n[[recall-corpus-name-boundary]].",
        "source": "mixing-embedders-in-one-tenant-is-silent.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-08-24T21:02:55.535401+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.665908932685852,
        "confidence": 0.9984332090672932,
        "verdict": "ok"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "ad407afb81ffbe3dd2ee8c1e07aded4d624969c80597ee525aca96a496c33bb3",
        "text": "`RetrievalDiagnostics.embedding_profile` (`recall/retriever.py:325`, `:471`) is **reported, never\nenforced**. Nothing in `recall/store.py` filters rows by it: the only occurrence is a `count(*)\nFILTER (WHERE NOT metadata ? 'embedding_profile')` used for a readiness report. So a tenant holding\npassages from two models is not an error state the code can see.\n\nIt is also not a *loud* failure, which is the part that matters. pgvector would reject a dimension\nmismatch, so two models of DIFFERENT width fail fast. The dangerous case is two models of the\n**same** width: `voyage-4` and `voyage-code-3` are both 1024, so a query embedded with one is\ncosine-compared against passages embedded with the other, the SQL succeeds, and the ranking is\ngarbage that looks exactly like a ranking.",
        "source": "mixing-embedders-in-one-tenant-is-silent.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-08-24T21:02:55.511114+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6136012625933847,
        "confidence": 0.986673421860014,
        "verdict": "ok"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "1bd4ead73b5ee728600f60c0ee6ba3fccfcd5296b5083ab003b1fc865cc9ac61",
        "text": "\ud83d\udd11 **Verify an embedder by `vector_dims(embedding)`, never by the profile label**: at least on\nthe fastembed path. Extends [[mixing-embedders-in-one-tenant-is-silent]]: the field that was\nsupposed to make mixing detectable is itself inert, so that lesson is stronger than written.\n\nNot filed as a fix yet. The fix is to derive the default `profile_id` from model name plus\ndimension, which re-fingerprints every fastembed corpus, a migration, not a one-liner.",
        "source": "fastembed-profile-id-is-hardcoded.md",
        "ordinal": 3,
        "indexed_at": "2026-08-24T21:02:45.717618+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5506235957145691,
        "confidence": 0.8472127190025408,
        "verdict": "ok"

        "text": "**The chunker is not in it.** So a file whose bytes have not changed is skipped even when the\nchunker that would now read it is a different one. Fixing a chunker-selection bug therefore does\n**not** repair an affected corpus by re-running `recall index`, the run reports \"N unchanged\" and\nleaves every wrongly-split chunk exactly where it was.\n\nTo actually rebuild, change one of the three terms (a different embedder, a different context\npolicy) or delete the affected sources first and let the next run re-read them.\n\nThe source docstring calls widening the tuple out as a migration rather than a comment change,\nbecause it re-fingerprints every indexed corpus at once. That is a real cost and the reason it has\nnot been done, not an oversight.",
        "source": "chunker-is-not-in-the-index-fingerprint.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-08-24T21:02:39.305953+00:00",

        "verdict": "ok"
      },

        "chunk_id": "47112135e2d9609b19470dcd40d54918f486c17419443b2ee34441310271f148",
        "text": "Found on 2026-08-15 fixing `recall index`, which chose the chunker from the GLOB SUFFIX\n(`chunk_code if args.glob.endswith(\".py\") else chunk_text`) rather than per file, so\n`--glob '**/*'` chunked every `.py` as prose and said nothing. Fixed by `chunker_for_path`, with\nthe non-repair noted in its docstring so the next person does not assume a re-index is enough.\n\n\u26a0\ufe0f `chunk_code` is **Python-specific**: it starts a block at a column-0 `def`/`class`/`@`/`async\ndef`. Given Rust, SQL or shell it matches nothing, returns one block, and is strictly worse than\n`chunk_text`, which at least splits on blank lines. Do not widen `PYTHON_SUFFIXES` without a\nchunker that parses the language being added.\n\n## Two consequences measured 2026-08-18",

        "text": "Measured 2026-08-19, in recall's own memory corpus, using recall itself.\n\nA memo carried a \ud83d\udd01 correction at the top of the file retracting a claim in its middle. Searching\nfor that claim returned **the falsified paragraph on its own**, as chunk ordinal 7, with no trace of\nthe correction: retrieval returns **chunks**, and the correction was in a different one.\n\nThe second attempt failed too, and this is the part worth keeping. I inserted a \u26d4 retraction\nparagraph **immediately above** the falsified block, re-indexed, and re-ran the query. The main checkout at\n`C:/Users/gde00/Documents/recall` usually sits on a feature branch (`codex/enterprise-rag-bench`\nwhen this was written), and **`master` is checked out in a separate worktree at\n`C:/Users/gde00/Documents/recall-suite-fix`**.\n\nSo `git checkout master` from the main checkout fails with *\"'master' is already used by worktree\nat ...\"*.         "text": "**A third form, same root: a squash-merged branch looks unmerged forever.** Squashing rewrites the\ncontent into one new commit, so the source branch's original commits are never ancestors of master\nand `git log origin/master..HEAD` keeps listing them. \"5 commits ahead of master\" on such a branch\nis not evidence of pending work.\n\nMeasured 2026-08-18: I merged master into `claude/enterprise-rag-dense-floor`, reported it as \"worth\na second merge before it goes in\", and only checked afterwards that its PR #334 had been **merged\nthree days earlier**, squashed as `6ce37b4c`. The real additions over master were 10 insertions\nacross 14 files, not the 4 commits the log showed. Ask the forge, not the commit graph:",
        "source": "bug-reports-from-stale-checkouts.md",
        "ordinal": 4,
        "indexed_at": "2026-08-24T21:02:38.665603+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5109475268062981,
        "confidence": 0.5200255660732765,
        "verdict": "ok"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "fa27fb6500f7e4329d99a67d0724b3f3793d582681c7d6d89e74dbd3836b58dd",
        "text": "Caveat when squashing: GitHub pre-fills the message with the PR title plus a bullet per commit,\nwhich discards the commit body. This repo's history carries substantial commit bodies (see\n`git log`), so paste the real body in before confirming.\n\n**A SECOND rule, learned 2026-08-12 by pushing one:** the ruleset also forbids merge commits on\n`master`. Pushing a local `git merge --no-ff` printed\n\n```\nremote: Bypassed rule violations for refs/heads/master:\nremote: - This branch must not contain merge commits.\nremote:   Found 1 violation:  f8e8f21...\n```",
        "source": "commit-signing-squash-merge.md",
        "ordinal": 2,
        "indexed_at": "2026-08-24T21:02:40.983791+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,

        "text": "**How to apply:** ancestry against `HEAD` is never evidence about master. Ask the question that\nmatters, at the START and again before merging, and read it as a supersession signal:\n\ngit log --oneline HEAD..master -- <the files you are about to touch>\n\nAny output means someone changed those files ahead of you. `git merge-tree $(git merge-base HEAD\nmaster) HEAD master | grep \"changed in both\"` confirms it in one more command. And when a commit is\n\"not an ancestor\", the next command is `git branch -a --contains <sha>` INCLUDING master, not a\nconclusion.",

To resolve: build a **post-exit pool reward-RATE source** (gamma per-market rate after exit), else close as NEEDS_DATA.\n- \ud83d\udd11 #1896 and #1897 are deliberately opposed \u2014 cannot both PASS. A PASS re-arms nothing (lane closed #1804, maker halted `_RMK_KILL`).\n\n## 5. \u00a72b deadman checks (local scheduled tasks)\n`gate-check-1895-2026-07-30`, `gate-check-1897-2026-07-30`, `gate-check-1896-2026-08-06` \u2014 each runs the gate-check + posts the verdict (run when the app is open / next launch).",

        "text": "**Why:** CLAUDE.md \u00a72b makes every gate carry a scheduled check as its deadman, but there is no\ninverse rule. An orphaned deadman is worse than a missing one: it arrives with confident,\nself-contained instructions and no knowledge that the lane died, so the default behaviour is to\nre-run a closed experiment and post numbers that invite a reopen. The scheduled task's own\nframing is stale data, not authority \u2014 [[feedback-verify-collector-terminal-table-2026-07-14]]\nis the same failure shape one layer down.",

On 2026-07-21 the `maker-net-tuner-gate-run` task fired for gate\n#1494 \u2014 closed 2026-07-16 with the LRP lane. The task instructions still read as a live gate\n(\"ahead of the 2026-07-21 gate\") and prescribed training + posting a learned-vs-baseline\nverdict.",

query.query: is it enough for a guard to refuse known-bad values

{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "outcome": "abstained",
  "answer": null,
  "clarification_request": null,
  "trusted_evidence": {
    "query": "is it enough for a guard to refuse known-bad values",
    "decision": "answer",

    "items": [
      {
        "chunk_id": "7627a6144867fa9a52b6d8fe0e77256ee89910be74868c79b4592c375ce411ad",
        "text": "**Refusing known-BAD values is a negative check. It closes only the failure modes you thought of,\nand everything the producer never emits \u2014 or that predates the field \u2014 walks straight through.**\n\nMeasured, RE-call `fix/beam-artifact-rejudgeable`, 2026-08-07. I wrote `embed_parity.py` to stop a\nGPU-vs-CPU comparison silently running CPU-vs-CPU. Three guards in it could not fire:",
        "source": "feedback-a-guard-must-require-good-not-refuse-bad-2026-08-07.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-08-24T21:03:36.308894+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6086865793092942,
        "confidence": 0.9837347979886707,
        "verdict": "ok"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "f4bf4e69226c1d8f0d47ec7979d99985a4c2181e97abba6416456adcf37f4ef5",
        "text": "\ud83d\udd11 The closed form is `if meta.get(\"providers_source\") != \"session\": refuse` \u2014 require the\nknown-good value. It rejects nothing the producer emits and everything it does not.\n\n\ud83d\udd11 **A test that hand-crafts an input the producer cannot produce is not a test of the guard.**\nThat is how #3 shipped green.\n\n\u2194 Same family as [[feedback-a-guard-that-reads-as-protection-and-cannot-fire-2026-07-30]] and\n[[feedback-check-the-deciding-cell-has-power-2026-08-06]]. What is new here is the *repair*\ninheriting the defect, and that only an audit by other agents caught it.",
        "source": "feedback-a-guard-must-require-good-not-refuse-bad-2026-08-07.md",
        "ordinal": 2,
        "indexed_at": "2026-08-24T21:03:36.350770+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5863803132033721,
        "confidence": 0.9602420294587457,
        "verdict": "ok"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "c7710c6887a9c186773a9eccd7880f412af38ce561ab97667e776db2de9699d9",
        "text": "- **A pre-filter may be sloppy; a decision may not.** The `case` in `settings.json` that decides\n  whether to *invoke* a guard can over-match harmlessly, because the script then decides. The script\n  itself cannot.\n- **One residual false positive is known and left in place.** Backticks inside single quotes are not\n  command substitution to a shell, but the parser treats them as such. It over-detects, which is the\n  safe direction for a guard, and it is documented rather than silently accepted.\n\nRelated: [[test-a-guards-allow-path]] is the same session's other half, a guard refusing correct\nwork. [[guards-that-cannot-fail]] is the opposite failure. [[a-detector-with-no-sink]] completes the\nset: fires and is discarded, fires wrongly, never fires.",
        "source": "parse-commands-do-not-match-text.md",
        "ordinal": 4,
        "indexed_at": "2026-08-24T21:02:58.252320+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5561231706215851,
        "confidence": 0.8742669910347236,
        "verdict": "ok"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "96aa1ae60e58ec857a9cb563932e57af50df5b00ac7e5b5ee3ce0c7e2ed9999b",
        "text": "- **Enumerate mutants from the SOURCE, top to bottom, not from the guards you remember.** I once\n  mutated 25 guards, reached 24/25 and called it verified; an auditor enumerated from the file,\n  ran 51, and 26 survived, including the identity cross-check the whole design existed for\n  (it compared one of its four columns) and a type loop whose deletion makes a bad row *served as\n  a hit* rather than refused.\n- **A guard with a long comment defending it is a positive signal it is untested.** The author\n  explained it instead of pinning it. `rollback()`, a `close()` on the refusal path, and an mkdir\n  block were each argued for at length and pinned by nothing.\n- **A guard with N conjoined terms needs N tests, one per term.** A single test can only ever see\n  one term, because it varies one",
        "source": "guards-that-cannot-fail.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-08-24T21:02:48.934773+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,

        "confidence": 0.7022969724136492,

        "text": "\u26a0\ufe0f Note the asymmetry that makes this dangerous: a cannot-fail guard produces a **false green**,\nand a cannot-pass guard produces a **false red** that discards good work. I produced one of each in\nthe same session.\n\nRelated: [[feedback-a-guard-that-reads-as-protection-and-cannot-fire-2026-07-30]] (the twin) \u00b7\n[[feedback-a-guard-must-hold-on-its-own-output-2026-08-05]] \u00b7\n[[project-recall-mtrag-retrieval-coverage-bottleneck-2026-08-06]] (where all three occurred)",

        "text": "Before deploying any sudoers lockdown that replaces wildcard `NOPASSWD: ALL` with a Cmnd_Alias allowlist, **verify whether the target user has a password set**. Without one, sudo for any non-allowlisted command silently fails with \"a terminal is required to read the password\" \u2014 the operator is locked out of every ad-hoc admin operation, and even console root login becomes the only recovery path.",
        "source": "feedback_check_password_before_sudo_lockdown.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-08-24T21:03:54.757426+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.7183369612198166,
        "confidence": 0.9998186118171875,
        "verdict": "ok"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "214c59a178ef664b6c20bd76bda001473723cd9034aeab6b53b32c125932d9bb",
        "text": "**How to apply:**\n- Step 0 (always): `sudo passwd -S <user>` (or `sudo grep <user>: /etc/shadow | cut -d: -f2`) \u2014 if it shows `L` / `*` / empty hash, no password is set.\n- If no password: ask the operator before deploy, *\"do you want me to set a password first (so non-allowlist commands prompt + work) or accept that the allowlist is a hard wall?\"*. Do not assume.\n- Even when a password exists, double-check the operator can recover via console \u2014 every Cmnd_Alias deploy needs a documented break-glass path that's been tested.\n- Keep the pre-deploy file backup at a path the new sudoers still permits to read (so post-deploy rollback to the prior policy is possible from the same shell). The 2026-05-05 deploy left the backup at `/etc/sudoers.d/90-sentiment.bak.<TS>` \u2014 DENIED to read by the new",
        "source": "feedback_check_password_before_sudo_lockdown.md",
        "ordinal": 3,
        "indexed_at": "2026-08-24T21:03:54.838004+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6555656585434472,
        "confidence": 0.9976038873164924,
        "verdict": "ok"

        "text": "Two pytest sessions running at the same time against the same test database collide. `tests/conftest.py`\ncalls `apply_migrations` from a session fixture, and `recall.schema`'s guard refuses the second one:\n\nrecall.schema.ConcurrentMigrator: another RE-call schema migrator is already running\n\nThe loser does not fail one test. **Every** test errors at setup, so the run reports e.g.\n`3 skipped, 62 errors` with no failures at all. Reproduced deliberately on 2026-08-05 with three\nconcurrent runs of `tests/test_bench_systems.py`: one passed, two errored wholesale.",

        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-08-24T21:03:05.654848+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,

        "text": "**How to apply:**\n1. A suite verdict is the SUMMARY LINE, never an exit code. An output file with no pytest output\n   means \"did not run or was lost\", whatever the code says.\n2. Launch long suites detached with their own log (`nohup python -u -m pytest tests/ -q > log\n   2>&1 &`, the `-u` matters or the log stays empty for minutes) and watch the log with a\n   Monitor until-loop for the summary line.\n3. Before relaunching anything DB-backed, list live python processes and match COMMAND LINES:\n   two suites on one session database invalidate each other silently.\n4. Distinguish your processes from other sessions' by command line before killing: this machine\n   routinely runs parallel sessions with their own suites.",

      {

        "text": "| Symptom | Cause |\n| --- | --- |\n| `ConcurrentMigrator` in fixture setup | two pytest processes contend for the schema-migration advisory lock; `scripts/ablate_store_latency_guards.py` documents it |\n| `LockNotAvailable: canceling statement due to lock timeout` | another session on the SAME container, still running |\n| `test_rate_limit_http.py`, `test_mcp_auth_http.py` | these stand up real HTTP servers and contend on PORTS; a private container does not protect them |\n| `FileNotFoundError` inside `tmp_path` | pytest keeps only the 3 most recent `pytest-of-<user>/pytest-<n>` roots and prunes older ones AT STARTUP, so a new run deletes the dirs of runs in flight |\n| pool / latency / backend-count assertions (\"pool churned: 3 distinct backends\u2026\") | CPU contention, not DB contention |\n|",
        "source": "concurrent-pytest-false-reds.md",
        "ordinal": 14,
        "indexed_at": "2026-08-24T21:02:41.179465+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.537134674958309,
        "confidence": 0.760933743895847,

      },
      {

        "text": "**Why it matters:** the guard is working as designed, but its failure signature looks exactly like a\ncatastrophic breakage of the code under test. It cost me a wrong conclusion once: in a mutation-testing\nharness I counted two mutants as \"caught\" because the suite went red, when the redness was this\ncollision and not the mutant.\n\n**How to apply:** run pytest sessions in this repo **sequentially**, never overlapping. In any harness\nthat shells out to pytest in a loop, treat `errors` and `failed` as different evidence: only `failed`\nmeans a test caught something. Retry (or abort) on seeing `ConcurrentMigrator` in the output rather\nthan scoring that run. See also [[bench-systems-suite-spends-openrouter-credits]] for the other trap in\nthis same file.\n\n---",
        "source": "pytest-sessions-cannot-run-in-parallel.md",

When a corpus wants a code model and a prose model,\nthat is two tenants, not one with two writers.\n\nFound on 2026-08-15 designing the `recall_repos` corpus on VPS2 (five repositories, code via\n`voyage-code-3`, docs via `voyage-4`).         "text": "`RetrievalDiagnostics.embedding_profile` (`recall/retriever.py:325`, `:471`) is **reported, never\nenforced**. Nothing in `recall/store.py` filters rows by it: the only occurrence is a `count(*)\nFILTER (WHERE NOT metadata ? 'embedding_profile')` used for a readiness report. So a tenant holding\npassages from two models is not an error state the code can see.\n\nIt is also not a *loud* failure, which is the part that matters. pgvector would reject a dimension\nmismatch, so two models of DIFFERENT width fail fast. The dangerous case is two models of the\n**same** width: `voyage-4` and `voyage-code-3` are both 1024, so a query embedded with one is\ncosine-compared against passages embedded with the other, the SQL succeeds, and the ranking is\ngarbage that looks exactly like a ranking.",

Extends [[mixing-embedders-in-one-tenant-is-silent]]: the field that was\nsupposed to make mixing detectable is itself inert, so that lesson is stronger than written.\n\nNot filed as a fix yet.         "text": "**The chunker is not in it.** So a file whose bytes have not changed is skipped even when the\nchunker that would now read it is a different one. Fixing a chunker-selection bug therefore does\n**not** repair an affected corpus by re-running `recall index`, the run reports \"N unchanged\" and\nleaves every wrongly-split chunk exactly where it was.\n\nTo actually rebuild, change one of the three terms (a different embedder, a different context\npolicy) or delete the affected sources first and let the next run re-read them.\n\nThe source docstring calls widening the tuple out as a migration rather than a comment change,\nbecause it re-fingerprints every indexed corpus at once. That is a real cost and the reason it has\nnot been done, not an oversight.",
        "source": "chunker-is-not-in-the-index-fingerprint.md",
        "ordinal": 1,

        "text": "Found on 2026-08-15 fixing `recall index`, which chose the chunker from the GLOB SUFFIX\n(`chunk_code if args.glob.endswith(\".py\") else chunk_text`) rather than per file, so\n`--glob '**/*'` chunked every `.py` as prose and said nothing. Fixed by `chunker_for_path`, with\nthe non-repair noted in its docstring so the next person does not assume a re-index is enough.\n\n\u26a0\ufe0f `chunk_code` is **Python-specific**: it starts a block at a column-0 `def`/`class`/`@`/`async\ndef`. Given Rust, SQL or shell it matches nothing, returns one block, and is strictly worse than\n`chunk_text`, which at least splits on blank lines. Do not widen `PYTHON_SUFFIXES` without a\nchunker that parses the language being added.\n\n## Two consequences measured 2026-08-18",

Searching\nfor that claim returned **the falsified paragraph on its own**, as chunk ordinal 7, with no trace of\nthe correction: retrieval returns **chunks**, and the correction was in a different one.\n\nThe second attempt failed too, and this is the part worth keeping. The main checkout at\n`C:/Users/gde00/Documents/recall` usually sits on a feature branch (`codex/enterprise-rag-bench`\nwhen this was written), and **`master` is checked out in a separate worktree at\n`C:/Users/gde00/Documents/recall-suite-fix`**.\n\nSo `git checkout master` from the main checkout fails with *\"'master' is already used by worktree\nat ...\"*.         "text": "**A third form, same root: a squash-merged branch looks unmerged forever.** Squashing rewrites the\ncontent into one new commit, so the source branch's original commits are never ancestors of master\nand `git log origin/master..HEAD` keeps listing them. \"5 commits ahead of master\" on such a branch\nis not evidence of pending work.\n\nMeasured 2026-08-18: I merged master into `claude/enterprise-rag-dense-floor`, reported it as \"worth\na second merge before it goes in\", and only checked afterwards that its PR #334 had been **merged\nthree days earlier**, squashed as `6ce37b4c`. The real additions over master were 10 insertions\nacross 14 files, not the 4 commits the log showed. Ask the forge, not the commit graph:",
        "source": "bug-reports-from-stale-checkouts.md",
        "ordinal": 4,
        "indexed_at": "2026-08-24T21:02:38.665603+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5110972841555993,
        "confidence": 0.5215636134099046,
        "verdict": "ok"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "fa27fb6500f7e4329d99a67d0724b3f3793d582681c7d6d89e74dbd3836b58dd",
        "text": "Caveat when squashing: GitHub pre-fills the message with the PR title plus a bullet per commit,\nwhich discards the commit body. This repo's history carries substantial commit bodies (see\n`git log`), so paste the real body in before confirming.\n\n**A SECOND rule, learned 2026-08-12 by pushing one:** the ruleset also forbids merge commits on\n`master`. Pushing a local `git merge --no-ff` printed\n\n```\nremote: Bypassed rule violations for refs/heads/master:\nremote: - This branch must not contain merge commits.\nremote:   Found 1 violation:  f8e8f21...\n```",

Ask the question that\nmatters, at the START and again before merging, and read it as a supersession signal:\n\ngit log --oneline HEAD..master -- <the files you are about to touch>\n\nAny output means someone changed those files ahead of you. `git merge-tree $(git merge-base HEAD\nmaster) HEAD master | grep \"changed in both\"` confirms it in one more command. And when a commit is\n\"not an ancestor\", the next command is `git branch -a --contains <sha>` INCLUDING master, not a\nconclusion.",

    "decision": "answer",

        "chunk_id": "c93653f255ee2ae29a525591bef4c4fbde14d7b4538c4aff652be10b04631946",
        "text": "funder wallet): `post_exit_7d` is a lower bound, so a low ratio is confounded \u21d2 NEEDS_DATA not a false FAIL. To resolve: build a **post-exit pool reward-RATE source** (gamma per-market rate after exit), else close as NEEDS_DATA.\n- \ud83d\udd11 #1896 and #1897 are deliberately opposed \u2014 cannot both PASS. A PASS re-arms nothing (lane closed #1804, maker halted `_RMK_KILL`).\n\n## 5. \u00a72b deadman checks (local scheduled tasks)\n`gate-check-1895-2026-07-30`, `gate-check-1897-2026-07-30`, `gate-check-1896-2026-08-06` \u2014 each runs the gate-check + posts the verdict (run when the app is open / next launch).",
        "source": "project-lrp-gate-work-2026-07-19.md",
        "ordinal": 5,
        "indexed_at": "2026-08-24T21:04:45.029078+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5554067061962699,
        "confidence": 0.870990047276813,
        "verdict": "ok"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "b1e319607401c01d2645d5614aa5f0cbf541a9dab0967c4b83f5c0d1c62094b2",
        "text": "**Why:** CLAUDE.md \u00a72b makes every gate carry a scheduled check as its deadman, but there is no\ninverse rule. An orphaned deadman is worse than a missing one: it arrives with confident,\nself-contained instructions and no knowledge that the lane died, so the default behaviour is to\nre-run a closed experiment and post numbers that invite a reopen. The scheduled task's own\nframing is stale data, not authority \u2014 [[feedback-verify-collector-terminal-table-2026-07-14]]\nis the same failure shape one layer down.",
        "source": "feedback-closing-a-gate-early-must-cancel-its-scheduled-check-2026-07-21.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-08-24T21:03:42.812501+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.613158840333189,
        "confidence": 0.9864318891365857,
        "verdict": "ok"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "87360cf238b9be73104d1ced608462149da32db54da70e47051274df296ecf84",
        "text": "**How to apply:**\n1. On arming any probe, note the **terminal table** the gate query reads (e.g. `polymarket_live_orders`, `*_fills`) \u2014 not the signals or dry-ledger table.\n2. Within 24-48h, run `SELECT count(*), max(<ts>) FROM <terminal_table> WHERE <edge_id/slug filter> AND <ts> >= <arm_date>`. Zero rows \u21d2 **not armed** \u2014 fix or close, do not let it ride to the gate date.\n3. Sanity-check the whole `systemd-analyze cat-config` view of the unit, not just the base unit file \u2014 drop-ins (`*.d/*.conf`) override `Environment=`, and a later `EnvironmentFile=` can too ([[reference_systemd_environmentfile_overrides_environment_2026-07-12]]).\n4. Every gate issue must have a paired scheduled check (CLAUDE.md Session-Close \u00a72b). #1594 had none, which is why it drifted 13 days unnoticed.",
        "source": "feedback-verify-collector-terminal-table-2026-07-14.md",
        "ordinal": 3,
        "indexed_at": "2026-08-24T21:03:52.487610+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5303836343035373,
        "confidence": 0.7068191025121813,
        "verdict": "ok"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "baa846d2844718d3a3590b39f318bec6071bfd8e1c5c3649e484e5d4abbb0d30",
        "text": "Closing a `gate` issue early (lane death, venue repricing, moot verdict) leaves its paired\n`/schedule` deadman armed. On 2026-07-21 the `maker-net-tuner-gate-run` task fired for gate\n#1494 \u2014 closed 2026-07-16 with the LRP lane. The task instructions still read as a live gate\n(\"ahead of the 2026-07-21 gate\") and prescribed training + posting a learned-vs-baseline\nverdict.",
        "source": "feedback-closing-a-gate-early-must-cancel-its-scheduled-check-2026-07-21.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-08-24T21:03:42.797565+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,

      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "e3c2c95967af3f2506d9a8d5867adf3d12d68c8a70c1f2d3197cf3308da501b5",
        "text": "**How to apply:**\n- Session-Close \u00a72c (gate resolved \u2192 comment + close) is incomplete: also **cancel or repoint\n  the paired scheduled check** in the same session.\n- When a scheduled gate task fires, **read the issue state FIRST**. `state: CLOSED` \u21d2 the correct\n  output is a SUPERSEDED note on the issue, not a run.\n- Do not treat \"the run is technically feasible\" as a reason to run. #1494's substrate was still\n  writing and the tuner still imported cleanly; the blocker was economic (`rewardsMinSize`\n  20\u2192200 priced us out), and no allocator result could move it.\n  See [[project-lrp-reward-farming-closed-venue-repricing-2026-07-16]] and\n  [[feedback-venue-can-reprice-you-out-overnight-2026-07-16]].",

query.query: is it enough for a guard to refuse known-bad values

payload:
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "outcome": "abstained",
  "answer": null,
  "clarification_request": null,
  "trusted_evidence": {
    "query": "is it enough for a guard to refuse known-bad values",
    "decision": "answer",
    "reason_code": null,
    "calibrated": true,
    "stale": false,
    "embedding_profile": "voyage:voyage-4",
    "retrieval_profile": "fast",
    "index_generation": "legacy",
    "items": [
      {
        "chunk_id": "7627a6144867fa9a52b6d8fe0e77256ee89910be74868c79b4592c375ce411ad",
        "text": "**Refusing known-BAD values is a negative check. It closes only the failure modes you thought of,\nand everything the producer never emits \u2014 or that predates the field \u2014 walks straight through.**\n\nMeasured, RE-call `fix/beam-artifact-rejudgeable`, 2026-08-07. I wrote `embed_parity.py` to stop a\nGPU-vs-CPU comparison silently running CPU-vs-CPU. Three guards in it could not fire:",
        "source": "feedback-a-guard-must-require-good-not-refuse-bad-2026-08-07.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-08-24T21:03:36.308894+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6082054739120896,
        "confidence": 0.9834149552284324,
        "verdict": "ok"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "f4bf4e69226c1d8f0d47ec7979d99985a4c2181e97abba6416456adcf37f4ef5",
        "text": "\ud83d\udd11 The closed form is `if meta.get(\"providers_source\") != \"session\": refuse` \u2014 require the\nknown-good value. It rejects nothing the producer emits and everything it does not.\n\n\ud83d\udd11 **A test that hand-crafts an input the producer cannot produce is not a test of the guard.**\nThat is how #3 shipped green.\n\n\u2194 Same family as [[feedback-a-guard-that-reads-as-protection-and-cannot-fire-2026-07-30]] and\n[[feedback-check-the-deciding-cell-has-power-2026-08-06]]. What is new here is the *repair*\ninheriting the defect, and that only an audit by other agents caught it.",
        "source": "feedback-a-guard-must-require-good-not-refuse-bad-2026-08-07.md",
        "ordinal": 2,
        "indexed_at": "2026-08-24T21:03:36.350770+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5863219253016676,
        "confidence": 0.9601501958096711,
        "verdict": "ok"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "c7710c6887a9c186773a9eccd7880f412af38ce561ab97667e776db2de9699d9",
        "text": "- **A pre-filter may be sloppy; a decision may not.** The `case` in `settings.json` that decides\n  whether to *invoke* a guard can over-match harmlessly, because the script then decides. The script\n  itself cannot.\n- **One residual false positive is known and left in place.** Backticks inside single quotes are not\n  command substitution to a shell, but the parser treats them as such. It over-detects, which is the\n  safe direction for a guard, and it is documented rather than silently accepted.\n\nRelated: [[test-a-guards-allow-path]] is the same session's other half, a guard refusing correct\nwork. [[guards-that-cannot-fail]] is the opposite failure. [[a-detector-with-no-sink]] completes the\nset: fires and is discarded, fires wrongly, never fires.",
        "source": "parse-commands-do-not-match-text.md",
        "ordinal": 4,
        "indexed_at": "2026-08-24T21:02:58.252320+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5560735464096069,
        "confidence": 0.8740423378130434,
        "verdict": "ok"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "96aa1ae60e58ec857a9cb563932e57af50df5b00ac7e5b5ee3ce0c7e2ed9999b",
        "text": "- **Enumerate mutants from the SOURCE, top to bottom, not from the guards you remember.** I once\n  mutated 25 guards, reached 24/25 and called it verified; an auditor enumerated from the file,\n  ran 51, and 26 survived, including the identity cross-check the whole design existed for\n  (it compared one of its four columns) and a type loop whose deletion makes a bad row *served as\n  a hit* rather than refused.\n- **A guard with a long comment defending it is a positive signal it is untested.** The author\n  explained it instead of pinning it. `rollback()`, a `close()` on the refusal path, and an mkdir\n  block were each argued for at length and pinned by nothing.\n- **A guard with N conjoined terms needs N tests, one per term.** A single test can only ever see\n  one term, because it varies one",
        "source": "guards-that-cannot-fail.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-08-24T21:02:48.934773+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.5293805756980354,
        "confidence": 0.6981927872242609,
        "verdict": "ok"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "7cccba84a63aff61faa5ebab8e33ae791b7c3f59f4b471028cf857fc54a7d386",
        "text": "\u26a0\ufe0f Note the asymmetry that makes this dangerous: a cannot-fail guard produces a **false green**,\nand a cannot-pass guard produces a **false red** that discards good work. I produced one of each in\nthe same session.\n\nRelated: [[feedback-a-guard-that-reads-as-protection-and-cannot-fire-2026-07-30]] (the twin) \u00b7\n[[feedback-a-guard-must-hold-on-its-own-output-2026-08-05]] \u00b7\n[[project-recall-mtrag-retrieval-coverage-bottleneck-2026-08-06]] (where all three occurred)",

        "chunk_id": "4b1dedd73c4c27960431e58ca07ea4fd44487560c6922906a49b54bf328badc8",
        "text": "Before deploying any sudoers lockdown that replaces wildcard `NOPASSWD: ALL` with a Cmnd_Alias allowlist, **verify whether the target user has a password set**. Without one, sudo for any non-allowlisted command silently fails with \"a terminal is required to read the password\" \u2014 the operator is locked out of every ad-hoc admin operation, and even console root login becomes the only recovery path.",
        "source": "feedback_check_password_before_sudo_lockdown.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-08-24T21:03:54.757426+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.718762993812561,
        "confidence": 0.9998217636750178,
        "verdict": "ok"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "214c59a178ef664b6c20bd76bda001473723cd9034aeab6b53b32c125932d9bb",
        "text": "**How to apply:**\n- Step 0 (always): `sudo passwd -S <user>` (or `sudo grep <user>: /etc/shadow | cut -d: -f2`) \u2014 if it shows `L` / `*` / empty hash, no password is set.\n- If no password: ask the operator before deploy, *\"do you want me to set a password first (so non-allowlist commands prompt + work) or accept that the allowlist is a hard wall?\"*. Do not assume.\n- Even when a password exists, double-check the operator can recover via console \u2014 every Cmnd_Alias deploy needs a documented break-glass path that's been tested.\n- Keep the pre-deploy file backup at a path the new sudoers still permits to read (so post-deploy rollback to the prior policy is possible from the same shell). The 2026-05-05 deploy left the backup at `/etc/sudoers.d/90-sentiment.bak.<TS>` \u2014 DENIED to read by the new",
        "source": "feedback_check_password_before_sudo_lockdown.md",
        "ordinal": 3,
        "indexed_at": "2026-08-24T21:03:54.838004+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6558352904270679,
        "confidence": 0.9976302648750723,
        "verdict": "ok"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "9c620896596e300a7d15f7d0fa88383421d7475d57437b5d89fd251092433b84",
        "text": "**Why:** 2026-05-05 redteam fix session. Saw `/etc/sudoers.d/90-sentiment: sentiment ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL` and assumed \"NOPASSWD\" implied \"no password set\". Deployed Cmnd_Alias lockdown. User immediately hit `[sudo] password for sentiment:` prompts when running outside the allowlist (e.g., `tee /etc/contabo/credentials.env`, `docker compose up -d` for a config refresh). The password actually *was* set, but the user couldn't remember it \u2014 equivalent to no fallback. Recovery options collapsed to (a) Contabo VNC console root login (operator did not have access at that moment) or (b) a destructive snapshot revert (the 2026-05-05 attempt got 400/404 from the Contabo API depending on body shape \u2014 `{}` body returns 404 'Cannot POST', empty body returns 400 'body cannot be empty'). The session",
        "source": "feedback_check_password_before_sudo_lockdown.md",
        "ordinal": 1,
        "indexed_at": "2026-08-24T21:03:54.783100+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,
        "cosine": 0.6403347253799438,
        "confidence": 0.9955248098780793,
        "verdict": "ok"
      },
      {
        "chunk_id": "8146703dfcd38c6c1fd3e38ca2da4c397dcaa57292dfbeba7b7c310bfdcc0800",
        "text": "**Rule:** On VPS (`sentiment@100.91.148.25`), the `sentiment` user **cannot read `.env`** and has a tightly allowlisted sudo. Treat the hardened workflow as mandatory.\n\n**Why:** Big security hardening done 2026-05-10/12. `.env` is now `root:sentiment-secrets 0640`; `sentiment` is NOT in `sentiment-secrets` (only `ftmo`, `chartapi`, `fundr` are). Sudo went from `ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL` \u2192 aliased allowlist in `/etc/sudoers.d/90-sentiment` (`SENTIMENT_SYSTEMCTL/JOURNAL/HEALTHCHECK_WRITE/READ_CONFIG/NETDIAG/AUDIT/DOCKER/PSQL`). Previous workflow muscle memory (`sudo systemctl restart anything`, `cat .env`, `sudo psql`, `daemon-reload`) is broken by design and must not be reintroduced.",
        "source": "feedback_hardened_vps2_secrets_2026-05-12.md",
        "ordinal": 0,
        "indexed_at": "2026-08-24T21:04:02.542736+00:00",
        "valid_from": null,
        "valid_until": null,

        "text": "`scripts/deploy.sh` does `${SUDO}mkdir -p '$BACKUP_DIR'` (line ~132) and `${SUDO}mkdir -p '$REMOTE_ROOT/$pdir' && ${SUDO}chown ...` (line ~144). On VPS2 with the sentiment user the sudo NOPASSWD allowlist (per `reference_vps2_sudo_allowlist.md`) covers systemctl/journalctl/PG/docker monitoring but **not `mkdir`** or `chown`. Result: deploy aborts with `sudo: a password is required` whenever the target subtree doesn't already exist on VPS2 (new research dir, new module).\n\n**Why:** Allowlist was narrowed in 2026-05-04 hardening pass; deploy.sh was written assuming broader sudo.
